# Study README Template

## Study Title
Neural cell screening models for endocrine disruption of thyroid hormone signaling 

## Study Description
Thyroid hormone is crucial for proper brain development.
Transmembrane thyroid hormone transport, intracellular deiodination and binding of T3 to the thyroid hormone receptor determine thyroid hormone action in target tissues. 
Chemical exposure can disrupt these intracellular mechanisms, thereby negatively influencing thyroid hormone homeostasis in the brain. 
To understand how chemicals affect thyroid hormone homeostasis and brain development, new screening methods are needed. 
We utilized different human-based in vitro assays to screen endocrine disrupting chemicals (EDCs)for their capacity to disrupt thyroid hormone homeostasis in brain. 

Human cell lines representing astrocytes (H4), oligodendrocytes (MO3.13) and neurons (SK-N-AS) were used. 
Thyroid hormone transport and deiodinase-mediated metabolism were tested using 1 nM radiolabeled thyroid hormone. Thyroid hormone receptor activation was measured using qPCR of the T3-responsive gene KLF9. 
12 EDCs were selected for testing, of which 6 were reference compounds used for validation and the other 6 test compounds. 

Reference compounds tested: sulfobromophthalein, iopanoic acid, lesinurad, NH-3, silychristin, xanthohumol 
EDCs tested: Amiodarone, cefuroxime, chlorpyrifos, mono-butyl phthalate, Polybrominated diphenyl ethers-99, Tetrabromobisphenol A

## Assays

1. Thyroid hormone uptake assay

Thyroid hormone uptake was assessed for all cell lines using radioactive [125-I]T3 or [125-I]T4. Compounds were added to the incubation medium together with [125-I]t3 or [125-I]T4 at the indicated concentrations.
cells were incubated for 10 minutes. Radioactivity in the cell lysates was measured using a γ-counter  


2. Deiodinase assay

Deiodinase activity (D3) was determined in cell lysate for MO3.13 and SK-N-AS cells. Cell lysates were incubated with 1 nM T3 and 200.000 cpm [125I]T3 for D3, 
and the indicated concentrations of EDCs or vehicle in PED10 for 120 minutes. Samples were analysed on UPLC (Acquity premier, Waters Chromatography B.V., Netherlands) coupled to a RAMONA star (Elisia Raytest, Belgium) detector.
D3 activity was expressed as fmol/min/mg protein. 

3. Whole-cell metabolism assay

Deiodinase activity (D3) in intact cells was determined for MO3.13 and SK-N-AS cells in the whole-cell metabolism assay. Cells were exposed for 24 hours to CT-medium, 1 nM T3, 2.000.000 cpm/ml [125I]T3 and EDCs.
Samples were analysed on UPLC coupled to a RAMONA star. The percentage conversion was based on %T1 and %T2 formed, in which %T1 was counted double because of two deiodination steps.
Data are expressed as percentage conversion relative to the average conversion in solvent controls. 

4. T3-dependent gene expression

Gene expression of KLF9 via qPCR in SK-N-AS cells. Relative gene expression was calculated using the 2−ΔΔCt -method. Data were normalized to GAPDH and shown as fold change vs. solvent control.  

## File Organization

Raw and processed data files are organized per assay.
